airspace.zh: 美國國家公園管理局自2014年起（政策備忘錄14-05）禁止在國家公園的土地與水域起飛、降落或操作無人機，大峽谷國家公園也適用；特殊用途須向公園申請許可。實際飛行前請先確認美國聯邦航空總署與公園的最新規定。
airspace.en: Since 2014 (Policy Memorandum 14-05) the US National Park Service has prohibited launching, landing or operating uncrewed aircraft on the lands and waters it administers, Grand Canyon National Park included; special uses need a park permit. Check the current FAA and park rules before any real flight.

tagline.zh-Hant: 1540年的西班牙人、1869年的鮑威爾，到1919年的國家公園
tagline.en: Spanish explorers in 1540, Powell in 1869, a national park in 1919

zh: 數千年來，大峽谷一直是原住民的家園。
普韋布洛人把這裡視為神聖的地方。
en: For thousands of years the canyon has been home to Native peoples.
Pueblo people regarded it as a holy place.

zh: 1540年，西班牙人加西亞·洛佩斯·德·卡德納斯來到這裡。
他是已知第一位看見大峽谷的歐洲人。
en: In 1540 the Spaniard García López de Cárdenas arrived here.
He was the first known European to see the canyon.

zh: 1869年，約翰·衛斯理·鮑威爾率隊乘船順流而下。
這是第一次有紀錄的科羅拉多河峽谷航行。
en: In 1869 John Wesley Powell led boats down the river.
It was the first recorded passage through the canyon on the Colorado.

zh: 在峽谷底的河段，激流一個接一個。
鮑威爾的探險隊有人中途離開，再也沒有回來。
en: On the canyon-floor reaches, rapids follow one after another.
Some of Powell's men left the expedition partway and never returned.

zh: 1893年，班傑明·哈里森總統把這一帶劃為森林保留區。
保護大峽谷的工作，從這時開始。
en: In 1893 President Benjamin Harrison made the area a forest reserve.
Protection of the canyon had begun.

zh: 1905年，鐵路公司在南緣蓋了艾爾托瓦飯店。
鐵路把遊客直接送到峽谷邊。
en: In 1905 the Santa Fe Railway built El Tovar Hotel on the South Rim.
The railway carried visitors right to the edge.

zh: 老羅斯福總統在1906年設立大峽谷狩獵保護區。
1908年1月11日，再宣布成立大峽谷國家紀念區。
en: Theodore Roosevelt created the Grand Canyon Game Preserve in 1906,
then proclaimed Grand Canyon National Monument on 11 January 1908.

zh: 1919年2月26日，威爾遜總統簽署法案。
大峽谷正式成為國家公園。
en: On 26 February 1919 President Woodrow Wilson signed the act.
The Grand Canyon became a national park.

zh: 1932年，建築師瑪麗·柯爾特設計了沙漠景觀瞭望塔。
塔高約21公尺，塔頂是南緣的最高點。
en: In 1932 the architect Mary Colter designed the Desert View Watchtower.
At 70 feet, its top is the highest point on the South Rim.

zh: 谷底的幻影牧場，是峽谷內唯一的住宿點。
徒步或騎騾子，要花大半天才能下到這裡。
en: Phantom Ranch on the canyon floor is the only lodging inside the canyon.
Walkers and mule riders take most of a day to get down.

zh: 北緣每年12月1日到5月15日因積雪關閉。
大約九成的遊客，都去比較方便的南緣。
en: Snow closes the North Rim from 1 December to 15 May each year.
About 90 per cent of visitors go to the more accessible South Rim.

zh: 1979年，大峽谷國家公園列入世界遺產。
公園面積約4,926平方公里。
en: In 1979 Grand Canyon National Park joined the World Heritage List.
The park covers about 4,926 square kilometres.

zh: 2024年，公園的休閒遊客超過490萬人次。
一個世紀前的鐵路觀光，變成了全世界的旅行目的地。
en: In 2024 the park received more than 4.9 million recreational visits.
Railway tourism a century ago became a destination for the world.

zh: 公園與三個原住民部族的保留地相鄰。
西邊的哈瓦蘇峽谷，是哈瓦蘇派族的土地。
en: The park shares boundaries with three federally recognised tribes.
To the west, Havasu Canyon is the land of the Havasupai.

zh: 從原住民的聖地、探險家的航程，到國家公園，
大峽谷的歷史，比人類的紀錄更深，也比國界更早。
en: From Native holy place to explorers' route to national park,
the canyon's story runs deeper than any record people kept.

tagline.zh-Hant: 原住民的家園，與二十世紀初的鐵路觀光
tagline.en: Native homelands, and the railway tourism of the early 1900s

zh: 大峽谷自古就是原住民的家園。
國家公園管理局列出十一個與這裡有歷史連結的部族。
en: The canyon has been home to Native people since time immemorial.
The Park Service lists 11 tribes with historic ties to these lands.

zh: 哈瓦蘇派族、華拉派族和霍皮族都在其中。
還有納瓦荷族、祖尼族、亞瓦派－阿帕契族和多個派尤特部族。
en: They include the Havasupai, Hualapai and Hopi,
the Navajo, Zuni, Yavapai-Apache and several Paiute bands.

zh: 哈瓦蘇派族至今住在西側的哈瓦蘇峽谷裡。
藍綠色的溪水，是他們名字的由來：「藍綠水之民」。
en: The Havasupai still live in Havasu Canyon to the west.
Their name means people of the blue-green water.

zh: 小科羅拉多河峽谷，對霍皮族有特別的意義。
這片土地，承載著部族起源的故事。
en: The Little Colorado gorge holds special meaning for the Hopi.
These lands carry the stories of where peoples began.

zh: 南緣東段的圖薩揚遺址，是古普韋布洛人的村落。
大約八百年前，這裡住著種玉米、豆子和南瓜的農人。
en: Tusayan Ruin, near the east end of the South Rim, was an Ancestral Puebloan village.
Some 800 years ago farmers here grew corn, beans and squash.

zh: 峽谷裡和邊緣，留有數千處古代遺址。
人們在這裡生活，比任何文字紀錄都早。
en: Thousands of ancient sites lie in and around the canyon.
People lived here long before any written record.

zh: 沙漠景觀瞭望塔的設計，參考了古普韋布洛人的石塔。
塔內有霍皮族畫家佛瑞德·卡波提的壁畫。
en: The Desert View Watchtower was modelled on the stone towers of Ancestral Puebloans.
Inside are murals by the Hopi painter Fred Kabotie.

zh: 塔建於1932年，設計者是建築師瑪麗·柯爾特。
她為南緣設計了多座融入地景的建築。
en: It was built in 1932 to a design by the architect Mary Colter,
who shaped several South Rim buildings to blend into the land.

zh: 二十世紀初，鐵路把遊客帶到南緣。
1905年開幕的艾爾托瓦飯店，就是為鐵路旅客蓋的。
en: In the early 1900s the railway brought visitors to the South Rim.
El Tovar Hotel opened in 1905 for its passengers.

zh: 南緣的大峽谷村，至今仍保留當年的旅館與車站。
峽谷觀光，就從這裡開始。
en: Grand Canyon Village on the South Rim keeps its early hotels and station.
Canyon tourism began here.

zh: 飯店旁的霍皮之家，1905年由柯爾特設計，仿照霍皮族的石屋。
1914年，她又在崖邊蓋了觀景工作室。
en: Hopi House beside the hotel, designed by Colter in 1905, echoes Hopi stone dwellings.
In 1914 she added the Lookout Studio on the cliff edge.

zh: 光明天使步道從村子下切到谷底。
騎騾子下峽谷，是延續了一百多年的旅行方式。
en: The Bright Angel Trail drops from the village to the canyon floor.
Riding a mule into the canyon is a way of travel more than a century old.

zh: 谷底的幻影牧場，是峽谷內唯一的住宿點。
北凱巴布步道從這裡過河，連到北緣。
en: Phantom Ranch on the floor is the only lodging inside the canyon.
From here the North Kaibab Trail crosses the river to the North Rim.

zh: 北緣比較安靜，冬天會因積雪關閉。
那裡也提供騎騾下切峽谷的行程。
en: The North Rim is quieter, and snow closes it in winter.
Mule trips several thousand feet into the canyon start there too.

zh: 許多遊客在南緣的觀景點，等待日落。
岩壁的顏色，會隨著陽光一分一秒改變。
en: Many visitors wait for sunset at the South Rim viewpoints.
The colours of the walls change by the minute with the light.

zh: 今天，大峽谷國家公園管理局與各部族合作，
讓部族的聲音，出現在公園的解說裡。
en: Today the park works with the tribes
so that their voices are part of how the canyon is explained.

zh: 對十一個部族來說，這裡是家園與聖地；
對世界各地的旅人，這裡是一生要看一次的風景。
en: For 11 tribes this is homeland and holy ground;
for travellers from everywhere, a view to see once in a lifetime.

tagline.zh-Hant: 從谷底到北緣，一天之內經過好幾種氣候
tagline.en: From river to North Rim, several climates in a single day

zh: 谷底海拔約八百公尺，夏天十分炎熱。
這裡是沙漠的環境。
en: The canyon floor, about 800 metres up, is fiercely hot in summer.
It is desert country.

zh: 科羅拉多河是峽谷裡最重要的水源。
河岸邊的植物，靠著河水生長。
en: The Colorado is the canyon's great source of water.
Plants along its banks live on the river.

zh: 從谷底往上爬，每上升一段，氣溫就降一些。
植物也從沙漠灌叢，換成矮林。
en: Climb from the floor and the air cools with every step up.
Desert scrub gives way to low woodland.

zh: 南緣海拔兩千一百公尺左右，長著矮松和杜松。
夏天常有午後雷雨。
en: The South Rim, around 2,100 metres, grows pinyon pine and juniper.
Summer afternoons often bring thunderstorms.

zh: 北緣比南緣高約三百公尺，降雨和降雪都比較多。
這裡長著高大的西黃松與雲杉、冷杉。
en: The North Rim, about 300 metres higher, gets more rain and snow.
Tall ponderosa pine, spruce and fir grow here.

zh: 帝國角一帶，是北緣最高的地方。
從谷底到這裡，就像從墨西哥走到加拿大。
en: Point Imperial is the North Rim's high point.
Going from the floor to here is like travelling from Mexico to Canada.

zh: 積雪讓北緣從12月到隔年5月中關閉。
冬天的北緣，只屬於野生動物。
en: Snow closes the North Rim from December to mid-May.
In winter the North Rim belongs to the wildlife.

zh: 北緣森林裡，住著白尾巴的凱巴布松鼠。
南緣的近親艾伯特松鼠，尾巴卻是灰色的。
en: The North Rim forest is home to the white-tailed Kaibab squirrel.
Its South Rim cousin, Abert's squirrel, has a grey tail.

zh: 峽谷把同一種松鼠的族群隔開。
兩邊各自演化出不同的模樣。
en: The canyon split one squirrel population in two,
and each side has taken on a look of its own.

zh: 1963年，上游的格倫峽谷水壩開始蓄水。
從水庫深處放出的河水，變得清澈而冰冷。
en: In 1963 Glen Canyon Dam upstream began holding back the river.
Water released from deep in its reservoir now runs clear and cold.

zh: 西側的哈瓦蘇峽谷，溪水呈現藍綠色。
水中溶解的碳酸鈣，讓溪床堆積出一層層石灰華。
en: To the west, Havasu Creek runs blue-green.
Calcium carbonate in its water builds terraces of travertine.

zh: 瀑布與水潭，是峽谷沙漠裡的綠洲。
這裡是哈瓦蘇派族的土地，造訪須事先取得許可。
en: Falls and pools make an oasis in the canyon desert.
This is Havasupai land, and visits need a permit in advance.

zh: 峽谷上空，可以看到體型巨大的加州神鷲。
1996年起，牠們被重新野放到大峽谷附近。
en: Above the canyon you may see the huge California condor.
Since 1996 condors have been released again near the Grand Canyon.

zh: 神鷲曾在野外瀕臨滅絕。
如今，牠們又能乘著峽谷的上升氣流盤旋。
en: The condor once came close to vanishing from the wild.
Now it rides the canyon's thermals again.

zh: 小科羅拉多河的水，在某些季節也是藍綠色的。
水的顏色，同樣來自溶解的礦物質。
en: The Little Colorado also runs blue-green in some seasons,
its colour again coming from dissolved minerals.

zh: 一條河，在乾燥的高原中央，切出一道生命線。
動植物沿著水，分布在峽谷的深處。
en: One river cuts a lifeline through the dry plateau.
Plants and animals follow the water deep into the canyon.

zh: 從谷底的沙漠，到北緣的森林，
大峽谷把好幾種氣候，疊在同一個地方。
en: From desert on the floor to forest on the North Rim,
the Grand Canyon stacks several climates in a single place.

title.zh-Hant: 一條河切開的二十億年
title.en: Two Billion Years, Cut by One River

tagline.zh-Hant: 長446公里、深1,857公尺，科羅拉多河五、六百萬年的作品
tagline.en: 446 km long and 1,857 m deep: the work of the Colorado in five or six million years

zh: 美國亞利桑那州的大峽谷，長446公里。
寬度從6.4到29公里不等。
en: Arizona's Grand Canyon is 446 kilometres long.
It is between 6.4 and 29 kilometres wide.

zh: 最深的地方超過一英里，約1,857公尺。
谷底海拔大約只有八百公尺。
en: At its deepest it is over a mile deep, about 1,857 metres.
The floor lies only about 800 metres above sea level.

zh: 切出這座峽谷的，是谷底的科羅拉多河。
它大約在五百萬到六百萬年前，確立了現在的河道。
en: The river at the bottom, the Colorado, cut this canyon.
It settled into its present course about five to six million years ago.

zh: 河流一面向下切，高原一面緩緩抬升。
兩股力量加在一起，峽谷愈切愈深。
en: As the river cut down, the plateau slowly rose.
Together the two forces drove the canyon ever deeper.

zh: 峽谷壁上露出將近二十億年的地球歷史。
每一層顏色，代表一段不同的環境。
en: The walls expose nearly two billion years of the Earth's history.
Each band of colour records a different world.

zh: 谷底最古老的岩石，是深色的變質岩。
它們在將近二十億年前，形成於地底深處。
en: The oldest rocks, at the bottom, are dark metamorphic rocks.
They formed deep underground nearly two billion years ago.

zh: 往上是一層層的砂岩、頁岩和石灰岩。
它們曾是海底、海岸和沙漠。
en: Above them lie layer on layer of sandstone, shale and limestone,
laid down as sea floors, shorelines and deserts.

zh: 最上面的凱巴布石灰岩，約有兩億七千萬年。
它就是我們腳下的峽谷邊緣。
en: The topmost layer, the Kaibab Limestone, is about 270 million years old.
It forms the rim beneath our feet.

zh: 峽谷寬闊的地方，是河流和支流長期侵蝕的結果。
雨水、霜凍與崩塌，讓谷壁不斷後退。
en: Where the canyon is wide, the river and its side streams have worked longest.
Rain, frost and rockfall keep pushing the walls back.

zh: 北緣比南緣高出約三百公尺。
地層朝南微微傾斜，所以北緣的雨水多半流進峽谷。
en: The North Rim stands about 300 metres higher than the South Rim.
The layers tilt gently south, so North Rim rain drains into the canyon.

zh: 帝國角是北緣最高的觀景點。
從這裡看得到峽谷東段的開闊景色。
en: Point Imperial is the highest viewpoint on the North Rim.
From here the eastern canyon opens wide.

zh: 小科羅拉多河在這裡匯入科羅拉多河。
兩條河的峽谷，在此交會。
en: Here the Little Colorado joins the Colorado.
Two canyons meet.

zh: 南緣東端的沙漠景觀，峽谷突然轉向。
河流在這裡從南北走向，轉成東西走向。
en: At Desert View, the east end of the South Rim, the canyon turns.
The river swings from a north–south course to east–west.

zh: 皇家角從北緣伸進峽谷。
峽谷內聳立的山頭，是還沒被侵蝕掉的高原殘塊。
en: Cape Royal reaches out from the North Rim into the canyon.
The buttes inside it are pieces of plateau not yet worn away.

zh: 從正上方看，河道在岩層之間彎彎曲曲。
這條河仍在繼續切割。
en: From straight above, the river winds between the layers.
It is still cutting today.

zh: 二十億年的岩層，被一條河在幾百萬年間切開。
大峽谷，是一本攤開的地球歷史書。
en: Two billion years of rock, opened by one river in a few million years.
The Grand Canyon is a history of the Earth laid open.
